ig_carousel_topic.topic: What 'units' actually mean (and why win % alone is a lie)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Your friend went 60-40 last month.
You went 53-47.
Guess who made more money.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most people track wins and losses.
Win percentage feels clean. It's also incomplete.
A 60% winner betting -300 favorites can lose money. A 53% winner at +150 can crush.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
What actually matters is expected value per bet.
Odds shape your return. A win at +150 pays 1.5 units. A win at -200 pays 0.5.
The price you pay changes everything.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: 100 bets at -110 (standard spread bet).
Break-even win rate: 52.4%.
If you hit 55%, you net roughly +5u over that stretch. That's what a sharp month looks like.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Units measure profit in a way win % never can.
Our YTD: 54.5% win rate, +38.3u, 9.3% ROI across 440 bets.
The number that matters is the last one.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win rate tells you part of the story. Units tell you if you're actually profitable. Both numbers live on our public tracker.
